newsitem.title: USA: Tower to buy A.O. Smith auto unit.
newsitem.headline: Tower to buy A.O. Smith auto unit.

text.p: Tower Automotive Inc said Monday it reached a definitive agreement to acquire the Automotive Products Co (APC) from A.O. Smith Corp for $625 million in cash.
The agreement is subject to regulatory approval. The transaction is expected to be completed early in the second quarter of 1997, the company said.
A.O. Smith said in a separate statement that it would have needed to invest substantially in APC to remain competitive.

"This sale will allow us to strategically focus and grow our non-automotive business and positions our automotive business and employees to remain competitive in the rapidly changing automotive supply industry," Robert O'Toole, chairman and chief executive of A.O. Smith, said.

Tower Automotive said it obtained a commitment from Bank of America N.T. & S.A. to provide the funding for the acquisition and ongoing operational requirements. Other long-term financing alternatives are being evaluated, the company said.

APC supplies lower vehicle structural components, assemblies and systems. Tower said APC had 1996 annual revenues of about $860 million and operating earnings before depreciation and amortization of $110 million.
APC's operations are based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin and consist of 14 facilities in North America and Japan.

"The combination of Tower Automotive and APC provides a strong North American base with global reach," S.A. Johnson, chairman of Tower, said in a release. "Our development efforts will focus on continuing our domestic growth in the consolidating stamping segment and substantially enhancing our global presence."
Tower is based in Minneapolis and provides upper-body structural chassis and suspension components and assemblies.
Onex Corp, based in Canada, has a less than 20 percent stake in Tower.
